questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following $\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{III})$ complexes, which one will have the highest octahedral crystal field splitting?
questions.solution:
A strong field ligand will enable higher crystal field splitting. It can be predicted from the relative position of a ligand in spectrochemical series.
In the given octahedral complexes of $\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{II})$ ion, the ligands are $\mathrmF^{-}, \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{NH}_3 and \mathrm{CN}^{-}$and their increasing order of field strength in spectrochemical series is
$\mathrmF^{-} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \lt  \mathrm{NH}_3 \lt  \mathrm{CN}^{-} \text{. }$
So, highest octahedral crystal field splitting is present in $\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$.

$\mathrmI^{-} < \mathrm{Br}^{-} < \mathrm{Cl}^{-} < \mathrm{NO}_3^{-} < \mathrmF^{-} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} < $$\mathrm{en}$$
Hence, among the given options,
$\mathrmI^{-} < $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ < $\mathrm{H}_2 $$\mathrm{O}$$ < $$\text{ en }$

questions.q:
The correct order of decreasing field strength of the below given ligands is

${NCS}^{-}$ $S^{2 -}$ $en$ ${SCN}^{-}$
$I$ $II$ $III$ $IV$

&
questions.solution:
The crystal field splitting, ${∆}_{o}$, depends upon the field produced by the ligand and charge on the metal ion. Some ligands are able to produce strong fields in which case, the splitting will be large whereas others produce weak fields and consequently result in small splitting of d orbitals. In general, ligands can be arranged in a series in the order of increasing field strength as given below:$I^{-} < {Br}^{–} < {SCN}^{-} < {Cl}^{-} < S^{2 –} < F^{–} < {OH}^{–} < {C}_{2}{O4}^{2 –} < {H}_{2}O < {NCS}^{–} < {edta}^{4 –} < {NH}_{3} < en < {CN}^{–} < CO$

Such a series is termed as spectrochemical series. It is an experimentally determined series based on the absorption of light by complexes with different ligands.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is tris (ethane-1,2-diammine) cobalt (III) sulphate?
questions.solution:
The given name is of cation type complex.
Thus, its formula is $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_3\right]_2\left(\mathrm{SO}_4\right)_3$ and is named as tris (ethane 1, 2, diammine) cobalt (III) sulphate. The following rules are used while naming the complex :
(i) The cation is named first (if present outside the coordination sphere).
(ii) Then, the ligands are named in an alphabetical order along with their quantity before the name of central atom/ion. (This procedure is reversed for writing the formula).
(iii) The name of central metal is written along with its oxidation state in roman.
(iv) If, name of ligand includes numerical prefix, then, the terms bis for (2) tris for (3) etc. are used and name of ligand is written in parentheses.
(v) If, anion is present outside the coordination sphere, it named without their quantity.
(vi) If the complex ion is a cation, the metal is named as the name of metal but, if the complex ion is an anion, the name of metal ends with suffix-'ate'.
(vii) The neutral complex molecules are named similar to that of complex cation.
Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

e.g., $\mathrmI^{\ominus} \lt  \mathrm{Br}^{\ominus} \lt  \mathrm{SCN}^{\ominus} \lt  \mathrm{Cl}^{\ominus} \lt  \mathrmF^{\ominus} \lt  \mathrm{OH}^{\ominus} \lt  \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4^{2-} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \lt  \mathrm{NCS}^{\ominus} \lt  $ EDTA $^{4-} \lt  \mathrm{NH}_3 \lt  $ en $ \lt  \mathrm{CN}^{\ominus} \lt  \mathrm{CO}$ :
Among the given options, ligand $\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)$ has highest magnetic field therefore, it has maximum value for $\Delta_0$. Hence option, (2) is the correct answer.

questions.q: A complex compound of $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ with molecular formula $\mathrm{CoCl}_{\mathrm{x}} \cdot \mathrm{yNH}_3$ gives a total of 3 ions when dissolved in water. How many $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ ions satisfy both primary and secondary valencies in this complex?
questions.solution:
As cobalt is present as $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ and co-ordination number of cobalt is 6 , the molecular formula of compound should be $\mathrm{CoCl}_3 \cdot \mathrm{yNH}_3$. Now, as it gives a total of 3 ions when dissolved in water, its structural formula must be $\left[\mathrm{CoCl}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2\left[\mathrm{CoCl}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2 \rightleftharpoons\left[\mathrm{CoCl}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\right]^{2+}+2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$
Thus only one $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ion is satisfying both primary and secondary valency of $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ in this compound.
